crop.notes: A crease runs down the left edge, clipping a few letters at the start of lines, but the text is readable.

ocr.notes: Names wrong: saloon keeper is Alex. McKee (not Mefgeo), Allen's second representative is Sherman Thurston (not Rinor); garbles the 'play or pay' clause; the last propositions were 'all rejected'; omits McCoole's 'repetition of the Coburn affair' and Allen's backers' unwillingness to put up a large sum; the closing rule quote is only partly transcribed.

summary.suggested: The Daily National Intelligencer, reprinting the St. Louis Times, reported that backers of Mike McCoole and Tom Allen met at McKee's saloon in St. Louis but failed to agree on a $2,500 match.

metadata.notes: Masthead: Daily National Intelligencer, Washington, Saturday, March 20, 1869. Article reprinted from the St. Louis Times.

facts.fact: Backers of Allen and Mike McCoole met at Alex. McKee's Broad Gauge saloon on Chestnut Street to arrange a match for $2,500 a side, but every proposition was rejected and no match was made
places: Broad Gauge saloon, Chestnut Street, St. Louis

facts.fact: Allen was busy superintending the opening of his new saloon on Fifth Street, St. Louis

notes: Exact date of the meeting not given ('last night' in the St. Louis Times); placed in March 1869. Fact 008 dates the Fifth Street saloon June-Aug 1869; this shows it opening by March 1869.
